Client's answers:
1. Yes — the system sends guias (claim forms) and treatment data to the insurance operators for billing purposes. Essential. → Confirm that integration under Art. 11 §4 is essential. In the deliverable, emphasize the legality of billing-related sharing (already handled) and make the Anexo (appendix) practical (don't let it block integration). Confirm that assumption (b) is valid.
2. NEXA uses AWS, "probably" in the US. → International transfer becomes an actual matter: need to tighten Art. 33 compliance in the DPA. The current A.6 draft already prohibits transfers except when there is Art. 33-compliant basis + prior notice. Given that AWS-US is "probable," it should be strengthened: (i) written confirmation of hosting destination; (ii) require SCC-style guarantees — caution: what does Art. 33 itself provide? Library excerpt: "transferência internacional somente é permitida nos casos previstos (país com grau adequado, cláusulas-padrão, etc.)" (international transfer is only permitted in the provided cases (country with adequate level, standard clauses, etc.)). So we can rely on "cláusulas-padrão da ANPD (ANPD standard contractual clauses)" as one of the cases — the library's "etc." covers the other cases; keep it general ("nas hipóteses do art. 33, com cláusulas-padrão ou equivalentes garantias (in the situations of Art. 33, with standard clauses or equivalent guarantees)"). Since the US adequacy is not confirmed in the library, label it as follows: the library does not state whether the US is on the "adequacy" list → unresolved matter; require NEXA to present Art. 33-compliant basis in writing before go-live; until then, the default is "domestic servers only."
3. Migration of 22,000 records will take several months; mid-term termination would be chaotic. → This heightens the importance of exit/lock-in: clauses 3, 10, and 7 become even more critical (renewal lock-in + exit costs). Also the migration assistance in the Anexo. Should the Anexo be updated to include "Migration & Reversibility (Migração & Reversibilidade)"? The migration is NEXA's onboarding phase (clause 1 includes implantação (implementation)). Mid-term termination being chaotic → the reason to strengthen clause 10's penalty clause (degressive) and secure exit assistance (already in A.10: 180-day export + transition assistance). Could add: interim export right at any time (not just at contract end) — data "portability" on demand + periodic export during the term (e.g., monthly/full dump at any time upon request) + escrow? This is a good, specific enhancement given the months-long migration. Also a "migration project" clause: NEXA's responsibilities regarding the import of 22,000 records (schedule, validation, completeness verification), and a provision that the implementation fee is tied to acceptance of migration? Be careful not to invent facts: the implementation of R$48,000 covers implantação per clause 1. Propose acceptance criteria for data import (integrity, completeness checks, sampling). Keep it modest.

The client answered Q2 (interest in aggregated use? No — only 3 questions were answered; "there is no additional information for unanswered questions" → mark unresolved matters explicitly). Q2 unanswered: default = no consent for NEXA's own use → maintain prohibition in the clause (our recommendation) — note it as a default assumption.

Updates needed:
1. clausulas.json — update rationale for clause 5 entry? Can add AWS-US fact to clause 5 entry ("FATO NOVO: AWS 'provavelmente' EUA (NEW FACT: AWS 'probably' US)"). Also clause 12 (AWS as sub-processor). Clause 3/10 rationale: months-long exit → strengthen. Clause 7 proposal: add interim export. Add/expand entry items? Add new "Anexo B (novo)" — a Migração clause? The contract says only list necessary changes in the json; a migration clause is genuinely necessary given "22,000 records, months of migration." Add one "inserir" entry: "Cláusula de Migração e Reversibilidade (cl. 1-A ou Anexo B) (Migration and Reversibility Clause)" at medium/high severity. Medium? Data migration of 22,000 records with TISS billing — medium to high. I'd say media (this is execution risk; the alta set remains data compliance). Hmm — but failure would be operational chaos; from a legal risk standpoint it's contract performance. Set as "inserir" / "media."

2. clausula_dados.md — adjust A.6 (hosting destination: AWS US "probable" → require Art. 33-compliant legal basis in writing before go-live; default Brazil until then), and A.10 (add full export at any time upon request during the term — supports months-long migration and mid-term termination chaos). Also A.5 list should include cloud providers. Small pinpoint edits.

3. nota_socia.md — update: new facts section (AWS-US: what it means — not a prohibition but an Art. 33 condition; who bears the burden; recommend written Art. 33 guarantees before migration, or hosting in Brazil). Update migration/exit section: months-long migration → 180-day period + interim export + migration clause + why clause 10's penalty clause matters (don't get locked into 36-month renewal when exit takes months anyway — actually the chaos argument cuts both ways: NEXA will point out Aurora is locked in; that's precisely why the exit plan needs to be contractual). Also update plan (dias 1-2: add Art. 33 request). Update "Deveres nossos (Our duties)" as needed.

4. QUESTIONS.md/PERGUNTAS.md — remove answered questions (1? Q1 price/units not answered; answered items were: integration essential (part of Q7), AWS/US (part of Q3), migration duration (new info, related to Q4)). Instruction: "don't repeat already answered questions" → rewrite QUESTIONS.md as remaining unknowns only, marked explicitly. Remaining unknowns: Q1 (units/price basis — unanswered), Q4 (legacy system and export format — partially: migration duration is known but source system/format unknown), Q5 (preferred venue — unanswered), Q6 (DPO name — unanswered), Q8 (NEXA's timeline awareness — unanswered), plus new: written confirmation of AWS hosting destination and Art. 33-compliant basis; whether NEXA already holds certifications/audit reports. Since the client says "no additional information for unanswered questions," the QUESTIONS file should mark remaining unknowns as assumptions rather than blocking questions. Rewrite as "DESAFIO — Remaining unknowns and assumptions" — the contract format assumes questions; the user said to mark remaining unknowns explicitly. Keep the file with a clear "Assumed default" for each item.

5. STATUS.md — update open items.

Plan: pinpoint edits per file. Keep output small. Start with clausulas.json edits (2–3 edits + 1 new entry), then clausula_dados.md (A.6 edit, A.10 edit), nota (insert new section + minor tweaks), rewrite QUESTIONS/PERGUNTAS, rewrite STATUS. Then do one final quick validation.

Given AWS-US "probable": add item 13.1: the hosting destination identified by NEXA is AWS, with servers possibly located in the United States; NEXA must (a) confirm in writing the precise destination and sub-processor (Amazon), (b) document the Art. 33-compliant basis (adequacy or standard contractual clauses/guarantees), (c) present until then or within the migration schedule… but caution: if no Art. 33-compliant basis exists, the LGPD transfer is illegal — the library lists only adequacy/SCC/"etc." The US adequacy is unverified → mark as such. Item text: "Até que a NEXA demonstre por escrito a hipótese do art. 33 aplicável... os Dados dos Clientes serão armazenados exclusivamente em território nacional; a migração de dados só terá início após essa demonstração (refletindo na implantação). (Until NEXA demonstrates in writing the applicable Art. 33 case... the Client Data shall be stored exclusively within national territory; data migration shall only begin after this demonstration (reflected in implementation).)" That's the core protection: no data goes to AWS-US before there's a legal basis for the transfer.

A.10 (items 19-20): add item 19-bis: full export at any time upon request during the contract term (within X business days, at no additional cost) — given the months-long migration, Aurora should be able to prepare an exit in advance. Actually add as part of editing item 19: "(i)...(ii)..."; add item "19-A"? Numbered 1..22; insert "20-A"? Cleaner: append a sentence at the end of item 19 + insert new item after 20 → renumbering is tedious. Simplest: expand item 19 with "(iv) durante a vigência, a CONTRATANTE poderá solicitar, a qualquer tempo e sem custo, exportação integral atualizada dos Dados dos Clientes, nos padrões do item (i), para备 migration and contingency planning." Append after the text of item (iii) at the end of item 19? The items flow continuously as (i)...(ii)...(iii)... "ressalvada guarda exigida por lei." Add a new sentence at the end of item 19.

Also add AWS as a named sub-processor to A.5? Covered in A.6.

- AWS "probable" US: the library does not state whether the US has an adequacy level (unverified) → practical rule: until written Art. 33 compliance, data should be kept in Brazil; block the start of migration until demonstration is obtained; don't rely on "probably."
- Migration of months + mid-term termination = chaos: that's precisely the reason (a) clause 10's penalty clause must not be 100% of remaining payments (you may need an orderly exit), (b) Anexo A grants export at any time and 180 days, (c) propose Migration & Reversibility clause: schedule, completeness validation, rollback with legacy until acceptance. So: keep exit tools contractual; also acceptance criteria for onboarding migration; interim dual-run.
- Billing integration essential confirmed: Art. 11 §4 explicitly provides for this; Anexo A.2 §6 enables it — integration can start from day one, nothing in the contract needs to block it.

Update plan section: add to days 1-2: "Art. 33 request (AWS-US)." Days 7-9 already cover technical export validation; mention migration schedule.

Rewrite QUESTIONS.md (new unknowns only):
1. Units/price basis (cap ambiguity) — Assumption: 3 units from start; "mensalidades" = total amount.
2. Preferred venue/DPO name/timeline — default maintained: no arbitration request; DPO recommended, name not identified; timeline maintained.
3. AWS written confirmation (precise region, Amazon as sub-processor, Art. 33-compliant basis, certifications).
4. Legacy system and current data format (for A.10 migration schedule).
5. Whether Aurora has consented to NEXA using aggregated data: default = no (prohibition maintained).
